properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/07/2021 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/07/2021
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 932873
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/07/2021
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess overall conditions on both pads. The drilling rig continues to operate on Pad B. I met with company man Bill Mitchell upon arriving on Pad B. Three small sumps have been installed in the pad surface since the previous inspection, in addition to the larger sump which had already been installed. All three are installed near the edge of the well site secondary containment and all three had stormwater in them during this inspection. One sump is on the north side of the pad not far from the original, larger sump. The electrical conductivity (EC) in this sump was 745 uS/cm. In the original sump the EC was 805 uS/cm. The sump on the east side of the pad, near the chemical tote storage area, was full of stormwater and the EC here was 718 uS/cm. The sump on the south side, closest to the company man trailer, had an EC of 516 uS/cm. The Department recommends continuing to pump out these sumps on an as-needed basis. No issues were noted on Pad B. On Pad A, multiple frac tank batteries remain on the pad within secondary containment. The wells are now fully staged for production. No issues noted on Pad A. Violations remain outstanding for the release on Pad B.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-01-02 to Range Resources Appalachia Llc in Cross Creek Twp, Washington county. 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Range Resources Appalachia Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-01-02
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 873590
Permit API: 125-28566
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Cross Creek Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-01-02
Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a follow up to a Restoration Inspection conducted on 11/12/2019 (See Inspection 2959521). Only the areas of the site associated with violations are being inspected during this visit. The Act 9 Sign is in place and appears to be in good condition. The access road appears to have various accelerated erosion rills along its length from the entrance to the pad. The Department recommends that the operator maintain the access road to prevent further accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring. The temporary storage tank appears to have been removed from the site. As a result, violation 78a.56(a)8 is being closed effective 1/2/2020. The interceptor channel 2 running to forebay 1 appears to have accelerated erosion channels. The Department recommends that the operator maintain PCSM features to prevent additional accelerated erosion from occurring. The forebay appears to be filling with sediment, which may be negatively impacting the operation of wet pond 1. The Department recommends the forebay be maintained to prevent an excessive amount of sediment from accumulating. It appears that the operator has put up some straw bale barriers at the discharge point associated with the riprap apron below wet pond 1 (mentioned in inspection 2959521) along with an erosion control blanket along the erosion channel to the edge of the LOD of previous accelerated erosion. Based on the Department's observation, accelerated erosion appears to still be occurring as water pools around the straw bales. Per the E&S Manual's Standard Construction Detail # 4-13 it does not appear that this corrective measure was constructed properly. Additionally, according to the E&S Manual on page 233, riprap aprons should be constructed at or near zero grade. It appears that this riprap apron is slanted to one side which is causing water to pool, and thus creating the accelerated erosion that is being observed at the site. The Department recommends that the operator maintain these features to prevent continued accelerated erosion. The outlet pipe for the under drain mentioned as part of inspection 2959521 has what appears to be riprap dumped over top of it and is still continuously discharging water which appears to be continuing to erode a channel through the field. The Department recommends that the operator maintain this feature to prevent continued accelerated erosion from occurring. Based on these observations the violation for the temporary storage tank will be closed. All other violations will remain outstanding.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/27/2021 to ARD OPR LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARD OPR LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/27/2021
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 924723
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/27/2021
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of a release of an estimated 5 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the pad surface on Pad B. This inspection was only conducted on Pad B. I met with EQT Company Man Bill Mitchell upon arriving on location. He showed me the location of the release which was along the edge of the well site secondary containment in the travel lane near the company man trailer. The area had already been scraped and backfilled at the time of this inspection. The company man said that the release had occurred from a radiator on a cement truck that was offloading into the upright cement tanks at the time. The truck was straddling the edge of the well site secondary containment so the fluid leaked onto the pad surface. The cement trucks were moved onto the secondary containment as of this inspection. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected. The sump that is in place on the opposite side of the pad surface has had a metal lid placed on it. This sump was installed after fluid with elevated conductivity was discovered by the Department in that area of the pad. The electrical conductivity of the fluid in the sump was approximately 1350 uS/cm. The area around the sump on the pad surface was dry during this inspection. Violations remain outstanding in association with this release.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8168591
Permit API: 059-24992
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Morris Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/15/2023
Comments: On December 15, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the WL Hopkins Well Site. The inspection was conducted in response to a request made by an PA DEP OGI during an inspection conducted on 12/15/2023 (Sub-SAIR# 3660126). At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Act 9 Sign Installed, however the Operator of Record does not appear to be correct. The associated PPC plan and ER plan on site have not been updated to reflect the change in ownership. (Photo 11 and 12)The COASTAL Drill Rig was on site and connected to the well. The drill rig and associated equipment was not placed within secondary containment. (Photo 1)I observed fluid on the well pad surrounding the WL Hopkins 590312 Well and drill rig. I also observed fluid within the well cellar. I collected conductivity readings of the fluid on the well pad and within the cellar, which result in elevated conductivity readings. I also observed what appeared to be a light colored crystallin substance deposited on the well pad rock adjacent to the standing fluid. The crystallin substance appears to be salt which suggest that the fluid has been on site long enough to begin evaporation. The amount of fluid on the well pad appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. At the time of inspection, the Department was not previously notified by the Operator of a release of fluid to the well pad. (Photo 2 thru 10)While I was on site, I contacted Operator representative Kevin Wright (CONSOL/Leatherwood) to relay my observations related to the fluid release and recommend that the Operator being remediation immediately. Mr. Wright indicated that the Operator added brine to the well to kill the well on 11/15/2023.I am requesting clarification of the activity, date and time of when the fluid was added to the well bore and all information/inspections related to the monitoring of the well between 11/15/2023 and 12/15/2023. I am also requesting clarification of the source of the fluid added to the well bore on or around 11/15/2023.Violation are being issued for the release (78a.54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301, 78a66(b)1,78a(b)1(i), 78a66(b)1(ii), 78a66(b)(2), 91.33(a) and 91.33(b).Violations are being issued for the failure to develop a site specific PPC plan and ER Plan. 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(c). 78a55(h).Violations are being issued for the failure to properly update the Act 9 Sign (78a55(i)(4)(D)(III).Violations are being issued for the failure to install secondary containment. (78a64(a))

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/13/2021
Comments: Inspection conducted in response to a complaint received by the Department of corroded production tanks and possible leak. Arrived on-site at approx. 1130 to conduct investigation. Well appeared equipped for production. No well label was observed on any of the production equipment on site. Recommend Operator affix permanent well label IAW the regulations. Well posting was present but has the wrong permit number on posting (Photo 3). Recommend Operator re-post with the appropriate and correct information for this well. Background conductance reading was taken in a field west of well pad (Photo 1). Conductance value in this location was 170 micro Siemens. Heavy corrosion was observed on production tanks. Holes have developed along the south and west sides of tank (Photos 2/4/5/8/9/10). A large hole (2'x2') has developed on the west side of tank. Production fluid/brine observed approx. 3" below large hole (Photo 5). Conductance of liquid in tank was 14,500 micro Siemens (Photo 6). Tank was located within earthen berm. Conductance readings were taken along the ground on the south and south-west sides of tank (Photos 4 & 8). Values were 3,740 & 4,510 micro Siemens respectively. These values were well above the background conductance reading and indicate a release of production fluid/brine onto the ground. Request Operator determine and provide quantity of release, the method how the quantity was determined, and the duration of the release. Recommend the Operator immediately remove all production fluid/brine from the production tank for proper disposal. It is also recommended that this production tank be removed and impacted soils beneath/adjacent to tank be delineated and areas impacted remediated. Production tank should be replaced once remediation is completed and confirmed by both the Operator and Department. NOTE: Conductance readings taken along the earthen berm were at background. It does not appear at this time that the release has migrated laterally. Violations are being cited related to the release of fluids to the ground and well label/posting. Pending Operator's response, additional violations may be cited.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an Administrative (ADMIN) inspection of the Seneca Resources - Cruttenden 846 Well Site in response to receipt of a NOV response from the operator on 5/26/23 regarding violations of SWMA 301, 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a) and the violation of CSL 402(b), originally cited 1/11/23 in IR#3486282 and 2/17/23 in IR#3506790. The NOV response state "Per your request in Inspection Report [3486282], non-reportable, de minimis quantities of higher conductivity fluid were transferred by field personnel and truck tires. Using the collection bottle for scale in Photo #13, the puddle from which sample 4427-298 was collected is approximately 160 inches long by 40 inches wide by 1 inch deep, giving a total puddle volume of 87 gallons or 330 liters. Assuming a brine chloride concentration of 115,200 mg/L (chloride concentration averaged across eleven different 26R samples recently collected from eleven different wells in Tioga County), less than 2 gallons of brine would be necessary to produce the reported chloride concentrations in the puddle. The 2-gallon volume of brine is likely an overestimation given that the calculation assumes all the chloride comes from the brine and neglects the appreciable contribution of chloride expected from road salt. The chloride/barium ratio of 765 supports that the puddle is enriched with another source of chloride as the Tioga brine chloride/barium ratio averages around 20 (as calculated from the 26R samples referenced above). Given that the pad material is sourced from the limestone of the Benner through Loysburg Formations at the Salona Quarry in Mill Hall, a quarry frequented by local mineral clubs for its strontianite, strontium leaching from the limestone and concentrating in the clay fractions of the pad material is not unexpected. There was not a release of a reportable quantity of brine.The puddle volume from which sample 4427-295 was collected cannot be estimated as the puddle from which the sample is collected is not identified. Photo #9 refers to multiple puddles with varying levels of conductivity. The reported chloride concentration for sample 4427-295 is 5 times less than the chloride concentration from sample 4427-298. The chloride/barium ratio for this sample is 2,697, indicating that the sample is significantly enriched by a source of chloride other than brine. This puddle is believed to be road salt transfer. As described above, strontium leaching from the limestone and concentrating in the clay fractions of the pad material is not unexpected. There was not a release of a reportable quantity of brine. As a prudent and diligent operator, Seneca reports all reportable spills/releases per the PADEPs regulations. Seneca Operations staff are working with field staff and contractors to continually improve containment maintenance and pad conditions after precipitation events, especially in the winter months when freeze/thaw weather conditions are prevalent."The Operator's response will be uploaded to eFacts and a Compliance Evaluation Inspection will be conducted to evaluate the remediation of the release.Violations of the following regulations are cited as OUTSTANDING against the Cruttenden 846 34HU, API#117-22129 :SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a)The violation of CSL 402(b), originally cited 1/11/23 in IR#3486282 and 2/17/23 in IR#3506790.

Violation ID: 902027
Permit API: 125-28620
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Robinson Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/10/2020
Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to a spill reported by the operator on 12/10/2020 at approximately 2:15 PM. The operator reported that an open top buster tank overflowed during flow back operations and approximately 20 gallons impacted the ground behind the tank. The operator reported a total of approximately 188 gallons total was spilled, with 168 gallons spilling to secondary containment. The operator is reporting that the spill will be remediated in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1). Nate Smiell and Brandon Carson with Range are on site, on my arrival. The following is observed: The site is currently in flowback operations (Photo 1). The pad drain has been closed. According to Mr. Smiell, he identified the spill at approximately 12:15 PM on 12/10/2020 during a routine inspection of the site. A time for the incident could not be provided at the time of this inspection. Mr. Smiell stated that it could have occurred anywhere between 12 and 24 hours prior to it being found. According to Mr. Smiell the open top tanks are to be inspected and the contents measured every hour. The Department requests these inspection logs be provided for the 24 hours preceding when it was found. Additionally, the Department requests the secondary containment logs for the past month, and at what time was the secondary containment remediated with the vacuum truck? Mr. Carson stated that it was possible that on-site cameras may have recorded the incident. The Department requests more information on this, whether they were able to record the incident and at what time the incident occurred if it was recorded. SPSI is on site and prepping to begin remediation of the site impacted by the spill. The Department requests photographs of the site post clean up as well as the waste manifest once it becomes available. The Department recommended to Mr. Smiell that the operator increase the length of the secondary containment (Photo 2 & 6). Based on this inspection, violations are being noted as immediately corrected. Pending the operator's response, more violations may be forthcoming.

Comments: On February 4, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management's Neilan 1 well located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4106039, where violations were issued for a release from a broken corroded pipe attached to the top of one of the production tanks on site. At the time of this inspection, the well site was snow covered, therefore, the vegetative cover of the well site, along with erosion and sedimentation issues throughout the well site and along the access road could not be assessed at this time.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the wellhead. Attached to this wellhead was a small metal production tanks, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of this production tank either. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed some production equipment and a meter box on site, inside the meter box was production paper dated 10/27/2023. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this meter box or the production equipment attached to it. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site that both appeared to be connected to the well. The tank on the left did not have any observable holes or corrosive parts, however, the tank on the right still had several corroded pipes at the base of the tank and a pipe that was completely broken in half due to corrosion at the top of the tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near either production tank at this time. During IR 4106039, the Department collected elevated soil conductivity readings at the base of the production tank with the broken piping. At the time of this inspection, the Department was unable to collect soil conductivity readings due to the ground being frozen. However visually, it did not appear that the release had been remediated yet due vegetation being overgrown around the production tank and release area.During IR 4106039, the Department requested the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of that inspection report. The written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, a plan for remediation of the spill or release, and how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requested the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon its receipt. To date, the Department has yet to receive the aforementioned documents. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from broken and corroded piping off of a production tank on site is remaining outstanding at this time.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr (Stepped) pressure build-up tests, (SPBUT) being performed on (5) of the (6) wells on the Cappucci pad. The Cappucci 4H, N 2H, 102H, N 4H and HJMM WYO 1H wells. The 2H is not involved in todays Pressure Build Up Tests. This is the 2nd round of SPBUTs since remedial Perf. and Squeeze work performed on the Cappucci 4H, N 2H and the 102H was completed on 6/14/22. SPBUTs were initiated on 11/28/22 @ ~ 10:00 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - The (20x13) annulus was shut in on 11/28/22 @ ~ 09:50 - 96 hrs - The progressive shut in for the (13x9) annulus was missed on 11/29/22, resulting in a 96 hr shut in for the (20x13) annulus - The (13x9) annulus was shut in on 11/30/22 @ ~ 09:50 - 48 hrs - The (9x5) annulus was shut in on 12/1/22 @ ~ 11:00 - 24 hrs - All (6) wells annuli were shut in at time of sampling. - Upon arrival I met with Creston Consultants reps. Jason Rajan and Dakota Manning and CALLC rep. Patrick Gardner. Starting at approx. 11:00, ending annuli pressures were checked using a Digital Crystal gauge. Permit API: 033-27255
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Brady Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/08/2024
Comments: Routine site inspection on May 8, 2024 with site manager Rob Platt. The Zelman UIC site is fully operational at this time but the site was idle at time of inspection. The last time this UIC received brine fluids was February 2024. Kendra Disposal is currently in contract negotiations with waste operators. I did a walk around site during the inspection. Please note, several areas of concern were observed during the inspection. The slope to the mechanical building has a lot of rills on the hillside resulting in erosion and sedimentation issues (photo 1). Compost sock has been installed to help collect run-off before entering into the truckers off-loading building (photo 2). The hillside has not been seeded and mulched per the E and S plans. This has been noted in multiple inspection reports since earth work started for this project over a year ago. In addition, the slope to the tank farm remains exposed. Rills are occurring on this cut-slope and sediment is collecting in the rock lined ditch. The cut-slope never had E and S blanket reapplied per the E and S plans (photos 5-7). The rock line ditch was never properly installed and/or completed after the tank farm pad was constructed. The rock line ditch just stops and doesn't connect to the sediment trap like is should according to the E and S plans (photos 8-10). Erosion is occurring along the access roads as well. Sediment is building up on the rock filters. Violations have been cited. The Department recommends addressing these issues.In addition to a site inspection at the Zelman UIC, historical background stream monitoring samples were collected at three nearby streams. Stream samples will be tested for SAC 046 plus lead and copper. These samples were sent to the Departments Lab in Harrisburg for testing. Results will be provided to the operator electronically upon receiving them.

Comments: On March 11, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IRs 4157087, 4157136, and 4157162. This inspection is separated into 2 inspection reports. The narrative of both inspection reports are identical except for references to photos. This is inspection 1 of 2. A COA with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, plugging operations have not yet commenced and there is currently no rig on-site. Earth disturbance for site preparation has commenced.This inspection is being conducted with Aquatic Biologist 2s Christy Owens (DEP) and Miles Hegedus (DEP) to identify possible streams and wetland along the access road.Culvert 1 crossing (Photos 1-2) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch. The outlet appears to be blocked due to soil moved during access road clearing.Culvert 2 crossing (P 3-4) appears to be a stream crossing. The outlet to the culvert appears to be blocked.Culvert 3 crossing (P 5-7) appears to be a stream crossing. The inlet to the culvert appears to be blocked.Culvert 4 crossing (P 8-9) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch, however this culvert is not receiving water at this time due to the operator disturbing the channel causing water to be diverted further down the access road (P 10-12). The source of the water appears to be due to a seep which is causing early stages of wetland formation. The disturbed channel appears to be carrying fine sediment (Photos 10-11) towards the stream at culvert 5, however no sediment was observed entering the stream due to the second half of the channel going subsurface with the entry point into the stream unseen.Culvert 5 crossing (P 13-15) appears to be a stream crossing. E and S off of the access road was observed during the previous inspection earlier today above the outlet at culvert 5, however no sediment is observed entering the stream at this time.Just past culvert 5 on the inlet side appears to be a wetland (P 16).Culvert 6 crossing (P 17-19) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch. The inlet of the culvert appears to be partially blocked. E and S off of the access road was observed during the previous inspection earlier today above the outlet at culvert 6. The erosion and sedimentation at this area appears to stop near the end of the culvert.Culvert 7 crossing (P 20-21) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch. The inlet appears to be partially blocked and the outlet cannot be seen at this time due to brush.Culvert 8 crossing (P 22-25) appears to be a stream crossing. CFS is observed to be installed and functioning properly above the inlet side of the culvert. Upstream from the inlet of the stream and near the soil stockpile in this area, the Department observed newly moved soil that has been pushed into the stream channel.The Department recommends the operator install CFS along the access road in all sections of E and S off of the access road and above each culvert inlet and outlet, as well as gravel the access road at all culvert crossings in accordance with the E and S plan.The Department recommends the operator install orange construction fence along the access road near the seep and wetland identified near the culvert 4 inlet and past culvert 5 (P 8, 10-12, 16).The Department recommends removing sediment from the stream channel at culvert 8.The Department recommends the operator restore the roadside ditch at seep.Violations were issued in IR 4157087 for accelerated E and S, for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, and for failing to maintain access road culverts in an inspection that was conducted earlier today prior to this inspection with Department Biologists. Therefore these violations are not included in this inspection report.New violations are being issued for sediment discharge into a stream, impact to wetland, and failing to identify wetlands and streams on the E and S plans.

Comments: On July 8 2025, the Department conducted an inspection of the McMichael Well Pad in regards to a spill that was reported to the Department on July 8 2025 at 9:12am . Present during the inspection was Brandon Carson.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Act 9 sign was posted at the access road entrance in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), and the Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan (PPC), both of which contained all required components, were located within the on-site mailbox. The access road appeared to be stabilized with gravel.Upon arrival at the well site remediation efforts appeared to be nearing completion as the remaining excavated material was being placed into the roll off dumpster. Mr. Carson identified the location of the spill. According to Mr. Carson, ,the spill (which occurred on 7/8/2025 at 7:15am) was reportedly caused by a 2" hydraulic line failing on the snubbing unit during work on the 14H well. This resulted in a release of hydraulic fluid to secondary containment as well as the graveled well pad. Mr. Carson estimated 50 gallons of hydraulic fluid was released in total with roughly 35 gallons releasing to secondary containment and roughly 15 gallons releasing to the graveled well pad. A vacuum truck was utilized to recover standing hydraulic oil. At the time of the inspection, Specialized Professional Services Inc. (SPSI) was onsite remediating the impacted area.Mr. Carson stated the contaminated gravel was excavated near the initial location of the spill approximately 6-8 inches in depth. Additional gravel was excavated in the area the hydraulic fluid flowed to at a depth of approximately 1 inch. The excavated material was placed into one roll-off box located on site. The Department was unable to obtain conductivity readings in the location of the spill as the gravel pad was too heavily compacted. However, the spill appeared to be visually remediated in accordance with the current regulations.Upon inspection of the rest of the pad, the Department observed 7 other well heads which appeared to be properly tagged and surrounded by protective barriers. The production tanks and GPUs onsite appeared to be within secondary containment with no visible fluid leaks or spills.Based on observations from this inspection and information provided by the operator, it appears that the spill has been remediated in accordance with current regulations. Violations are being issued as immediately corrected for the release of hydraulic fluid outside of secondary containment.

Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC

Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 8181535
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 3/29/2024
Comments: On 3/29/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an admin inspection for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection is to report the results of two water samples that were collected during drilling operations from two different locations at the site.During inspection #3724668 conducted on 3/6/2024, the department discovered instances of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad surface and in the sediment basin below the north side of the pad. On 3/27/2024, the department received the results of the samples. Sample 9551-087 was collected from a channel of water along the north perimeter berm that appeared to have a white substance along the length of it. The water field tested at 4.10 mS conductance. The puddle was near the outfall leading to the sediment basin and was approximately 60 feet long and ranged from 6 inches to 2 feet wide and up to 1.5 inches deep. A 2 inch wide by 1 inch deep stream of water was flowing down the outfall that field tested at 4.11 mS conductance. The water was flowing down to the northeast end of the sediment basin. The results are shown in pictures 1 and 2. Sample 9551-088 was collected from the sediment basin where a white plume was visible leading into the sediment basin coming from the rock outfall leading off the pad. The flow of water leading into the sediment basin from the pad field tested at 2.48 mS conductance. The results are shown in pictures 3 and 4.Noted during inspection #3724668, water leaving the sediment basin field tested at 1.156 mS conductance. Water flowing off location field tested at 1.084 mS conductance. During previous inspections, water flowing in a channel below the northeast corner of the pad and below the sediment basin field tested at 0.3 mS conductance or less.The samples show elevated levels of aluminum, iron, chlorides and strontium which indicates the release of a pollutional substance on the pad and reaching the basin.During inspection 3704886 conducted on 1/29/2023, sample 9551-080 was collected from a channel of water along the northeast cornerof the pad that field tested at 4.2 mS conductance. The laboratory analysis of the sample showed elevated levels of pH, calcium, iron, chlorides and strontium as shown in pictures 5 and 6. Bags of deicing media was reported as being applied near this area.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface and into the sedimentation basin constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78a.66(b)(2).This incident has the potential to cause pollution as defined by 25 PA Code 93.6(a), 25 PA Code 93.6(b), and 25 PA Code 91.33(a) and does not meet the discharge requirements under 25 PA Code 78a.60(b).Because of the large volume of elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface and in the sedimentation basin, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3724668 for a 6' x 60' puddle of water with elevated conductance and with a white substance in it; discovered on the unprotected pad surface and flowing into the sediment basin during drilling operations.The DEP recommends the following: 1. The department recommends that Seneca determine the source of the white substance, elevated conductance, pH, aluminum, iron, and strontium in the water sample and take measures to address it, including but not limited to; ceasing discharge, collecting the water for reuse/disposal, etc.2. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid at the north side of the pad and the basin; clean/report as necessary.

Report Details

Inspection Date: 8/19/2026
Comments: On August 19, 2026, the Department conducted a complaint inspection of the Cecil 2-P229 OG Well in regard to CTS 400392.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department did not observe an Act 9 sign. The Department recommends the operator install an Act 9 sign in accordance with 78a55. The Department also did not observe an Emergency Response Plan (ERP). The Department recommends the operator ensure an ERP is onsite in accordance with 78a55.At the time of the inspection the well was located in an open agricultural field. The access road appeared stabilized. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.Upon inspection of the production equipment, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag and well posting were present onsite appeared to have all information in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H). There were no observed leaks or discharges of fluid at the surface around the wellhead.There appeared to be 3 total production tanks onsite. Upon further inspection, it appeared the white poly tank was connected and in use. The tank appeared to be in sound condition with no observed leaks or discharges of fluid were observed around this tank.Two metal tanks were also present onsite but did not appear to be in use at the time of the inspection. Upon further inspection of the 2 metal tanks, one of the tanks appeared to be severely corroded with multiple holes in the tank observed. The Department observed fluid flowing down the side of the tank. A conductivity reading of this fluid was obtained and was "OR" (Over detectable range, >20mS). Upon inspection of the ground surrounding the corroded production tank, the Department observed orange staining and saturated dirt/gravel. Conductivity readings were taken in the area of staining and saturation with readings of 12.78mS, 9.24mS, 4.37mS, and 1.82mS being obtained. These readings are elevated in comparison to the background conductivity reading obtained of 0.19mS. Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings, it appears a release has/is occurring from the corroded production tank.Prior to leaving the site, the Department spoke with operator representative Robert Inghram and informed him of the Department's observations of an apparent release. Mr. Inghram stated the metal tanks have been disconnected and empty for several years. The Department recommended remediation of the spill and removal of the production tanks as they are no longer in use and heavily corroded. Mr. Inghram stated he would get a contractor to begin the work as soon as possible.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release, production equipment onsite not in use, no ERP onsite, and no Act 9 Sign onsite.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8249068
Permit API: 129-24019
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/15/2025
Comments: On September 15 2025, the Department conducted an inspection of the E Shuster 2 OG Well in response to an OGI referral of the production tank leaking what appeared to be production fluid.At the time of inspection, the well appeared to drilled and equipped for production. The well tag was present on the well head. During the inspection, it appeared the production tank had previously been leaking and/or overflowed, but did not appear to be actively leaking. The tank appeared to be approximately 80% full at the time of the inspection.At the base of the production tank, there appeared to be an excess amount of fluid along with a thick oil based matter. There appeared to be absorbent mats on the ground next to and under the production tank where the release appeared to have occurred. Based on the amount of fluid on the ground observed by the Department, this appeared to be a reportable release (5 gallons or more). A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.05mS. Conductivity readings were taken in the soil in the area of the spill. While some readings appeared comparable to the background reading, others were elevated in comparison to the background reading. Readings of 0.09mS 0.10mS, 0.14mS 0.31mS, 0.39mS, 0.41mS, 0.49ms, 0.64mS, 1.39mS, 1.33mS were obtained by the Department. Elevated readings were detected in about a 1 foot radius around the production tank.Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted operator representative Joe Miller to inform him of the release. Mr. Miller indicated that they had replaced/repaired a faulty dump valve the week prior. He stated field members would be at the site to assess the area for a release and remediation would occur as necessary. The Department recommended that the Operator take immediate action to remediate the area in accordance with the Department's current spill policy.The operator is requested to submit a written response within 7 days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include:1.) An incident report including the quantity and type of fluid released (including the oil based matter) and how this was determined.2.) How long it is believed the release was occurring,3.) A timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.4.) Clarification/waste manifests for any production fluid or other production waste that has been disposed of from the site in the last 2 years.The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the failure to properly control production fluid (and/or other fluids) resulting in a release to the ground, as well as failure to report a release.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#302235). This well is located approximately 1,377ft NE from the complainants water well. The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, and possible failures. The well is equipped for production and is currently producing off of the 1 1/2" tubing. The well is equipped with a required check valve. Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation and are current. As part of the investigation 4 slam bar holes were placed into the ground in the cardinal directions approximately 6" to 1' from the well-head and approximately 3' deep to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. A Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II gas meter which was calibrated on 05/06/2024 was used to take the soil gas readings. In the East slam bar hole a soil gas reading of 12% LEL was observed. ( See attached PHOTO 8). As a result of the soil gas readings in the east slam bar hole the following violations are being placed against this well: VIOLATION:78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected. VIOLATION:78.73(b) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to prevent gas, oil, brine, completion, and servicing fluids, and any other fluids or materials from below the casing seat from entering fresh groundwater, and prevent pollution or diminution of fresh groundwater. VIOLATION: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING – DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. VIOLATION:78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS – MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well. At this time that apartment is requesting an investigation into the possible source of methane to be conducted by the operator.

Violation ID: 976075
Permit API: 015-23708
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Asylum Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/16/2022
Comments: On 11/16/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident/response to accident or event inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. This inspection is in response to Complaint Id 368309 for one barrel of brine water spilled outside of secondary containment from a frac tank on the site.Prior to my arrival, Chesapeake's Danielle Schaad informed me that the frac tank would be to the right when arriving on site and was stationed in secondary containment by itself. She said that the location of the leak in the frac tank and in the secondary containment was unknown but high conductance water was discovered outside of secondary containment on the pad surface. She said that the fluid was brine water from the produced water tank. She reported that the tank and secondary containment had been emptied and the puddle vacuumed up. She said that the tank was being removed from location and that Cresson Environmental would be onsite on 11/17/2022. It was 40 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. Heavy snowfall had impacted the region in the last 24 hours and was melting with the pad being mostly clear of snow. A skid steer and a vac truck had just arrived on location and were setting up next to a frac tank in the northeast corner of the site. The frac tank was still connected to the 1HC gas well GPU. A crew was working on disconnecting it from the GPU. A vac box was located south of the frac tank. I field tested various water puddles in close proximity to the frac tank for conductance using an Oakton PCTS 50 with an upper limit of 20.0 mS with the following results: 40'x 40' water puddle on the south west corner of the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 0.77 mS.5' x 8' water puddle outside the southeast corner of the vac box field tested at 14.43 mS.20' x 20' water puddle southeast of the frac tank secondary containment was over 20.0 mS.15 x 30' water puddle east of the frac tank secondary containment was over 20.0 mS.6' x 20' water puddle northeast of the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 3.53 mS.12' x 40' water puddle on the east edge of the site above the recently excavated fill slope field tested at 2.33 mS.Water below the rocked section of the fill slope field tested at 1.20 mS. Water in the south end of infiltration area 1 field tested at 1.40 mS.Other water puddles on the pad surface field tested at 0.8 mS or less.There were ten wells staged for production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. A rainbow sheen was witnessed in the Hopson 101HC, 22HC, 4HC and 5H well cellars. Six of the GPUs and the production tank had secondary containment. There were six frac tanks and one gas buster staged in secondary containment on the west side of location. While on site the frac tank with the suspected leak and the secondary containment were removed from location. Water puddles adjacent to the frac tank location were vacuumed up. Joe Button discussed that an excavator will be brought to location along with Creston Environmental to conduct cleanup operations at 0800 hrs on 11/17/2022. This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 56[a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b)The DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a 66(c)The department also recommends removing the water from and cleaning the well cellars noted for having sheens; the Hopson 101HC, 22HC, 4HC and 5H well cellars.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3406647 for high conductance fluid escaping from damaged containment during well stimulation activities with an unknown volume impacting the pad surface.I left the site at 1400 hours.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the JKLM Sweden Valley 107 well pad located in Sweden Twp, Potter Co. on 6/3/2019 @1115 hours in response to notification of a spill, reported to the Department on 5/31/2019 @1535 hours. The weather was sunny, 54 degrees, winds WSW 5mph, gusts 10mph. Present onsite for the inspection were Terra Tokarz, Whipper Hill Consulting and Matt Skolny, JKLM. CTS report# 342615 states, JKLM reported a hose broke while pumping production water from the production water tank to the tank farm releasing approximately 3 to 4 barrels of production water; released water overwhelmed pump containment and spilled to gravel (soil/concrete) surface; JKLM utilized on-site vac truck to recover fluid. The following onsite conditions were observed during the inspection. The pump had been moved approximately 15' from the original spill location in order to allow for excavation of pad material impacted during the spill. Onsite personnel stated a valve, on a pump component, was left open while the operator traveled to another site to check on a different water transfer. This allowed the suction line from the pump to discharge production fluid, from the production tanks on the SV107, into it's secondary containment. The fluid over-topped the containment discharging an estimated 3 barrels of production fluid onto the pad surface. The fluid was recovered with a vacuum truck. Approximately 2-4" of pad material in a 35' x 70' area was excavated after a grid screening for conductivity, and placed in waste containers onsite. Penn E&R arrived onsite to collect confirmatory samples during the inspection. Violations of the following regulations are cited at this time: 25 Pa Code 78a.57 CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 I departed the site at 1245 hours.
